newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Switzerland's Swiss Bank Corp. to buy Dillon Read.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland's Swiss Bank Corp. to buy Dillon Read.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp., moving to expand its role in U.S. investment banking, said Thursday it agreed to buy Dillon Read & Co. for about $600 million.

Speculation of an SBC deal grew after Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV, which owns 25 percent of Dillion Read, said Wednesday it broke off talks to buy the remaining 75 percent from the firm's partners.

The Swiss banking giant said that upon completion of the deal, which is subject to approval by the U.S. Federal Reserve and other regulators, Dillon Read would be merged with SBC Warburg, SBC's investment banking and capital markets division. The combined entity would be known as SBC Warburg Dillon Read.
SBC acquired S.G. Warburg in mid-1995.

SBC Chief Executive Marcel Ospel had said last month that the company had no plans for a major investment banking acquisition in North America. He also dismissed the idea of buying a second-tier U.S. investment bank, but said his bank would consider acquiring a franchise or expertise through the purchase of a small boutique.

Dillon Read is not a major player and its acquisition is not expected immediately to push SBC to the top of the heap in the U.S. investment banking community, analysts said. But Dillon has a good reputation, a good client book and capable management, they added.
"The key relationships (with Dillion management and their corporate finance contacts) will make or break the deal," Salomon Brothers banking analyst John Leonard said prior to SBC's announcement.
SBC said it would finance the deal with existing stock and that it would "not result in a material dilution of earnings."

"The combination of Dillon Read's extremely high quality advisory franchise and focused expertise in both debt and equity markets in the United States, together with SBC Warburg's own strength in Europe, Latin America and Australasia will create enormous benefits for our clients and shareholders alike," SBC Warburg Chairman Hans de Gier said in a statement.
Dillon Read has 730 employees. In 1996 it completed 50 mergers and acquisitions worth $45 billion. It is also active in the high-yield, equity and private placement markets.
